title: review: S2d2 cache-aware tool and skill disclosure in shadow: stable Level-0 tool catalog view and stable skill catalog block, measured on the existing tool_disclosure and skill_selection rows (P9, P10)
spec:
orchestrator/tool_catalog.py exposes a pure function cache_view(role, keep, previous_row) returning {stable_catalog_chars (the Level-0 catalog: names and one-line purposes of every known tool for the role, identical across tasks), dynamic_chars (the selected Level-2 schemas), changed_since_previous (True, False, or None when previous_row is None)}; orchestrator/bus.py (scope), where tool_disclosure rows are written (near line 285), calls it and stores the three fields on the row; previous_row is the last tool_disclosure row of the same role among the most recent 200 decision_log rows (bounded read, no module state). Active presentation ([tool_disclosure].cache_mode active): the stable catalog text precedes the dynamic schemas in the tool disclosure text built for the packet. Skills: orchestrator/skill_router.py exposes catalog_block(role, registry) (sorted ids and triggers of every active skill for the role, identical across tasks); orchestrator/spawn.py (scope), where _prepare_skills builds the presented skills section, prepends that block ONLY when [skills].cache_mode is active, and always records catalog_chars and selected_chars on the existing skill_selection row. Both sections get cache_mode = "shadow" with dated comments and revert instructions, missing key means off, validated in pool (S2d1 adds the validation helper; reuse it), inert when the section's mode is off. Docs: sections 2 and 3 of docs/hermes-hardening/10-cache-aware-disclosure.md with a reproducible command (`orchestrator scorecard --economy --disclosure-cache`, scope orchestrator/cli.py) printing row counts, date range, mean stable vs dynamic chars and the share of runs whose dynamic list changed since the previous task of the role; when no rows exist the doc says so.
Spec review T-1293 folded in: (1) One helper, two callers: tool_catalog.cache_view(role, kept_ids, previous_row) is pure; the two existing tool_disclosure row writers call it: spawn._shadow_tool_disclosure (Claude roles) and bus.log_run's Codex row; the escalation row (reason hidden_tool_requested) is left untouched and never used as a previous row. (2) previous_row = the most recent tool_disclosure row for the same role whose subject is a DIFFERENT task and which carries deterministic.kept; found through a new bounded helper decision_log.last_row(kind, *, role, exclude_subject, require_key) that reads only today's decision_log file from the end (scope adds orchestrator/decision_log.py and tests/test_decision_log.py); an older row without the new fields still qualifies as previous when it has kept; none found -> changed_since_previous None. (3) changed_since_previous compares the SETS of kept ids (order ignored). (4) Level-0 catalog = tool_catalog.level0(ids) rendered as one line per tool (name and purpose) over the role's static disclosed id list (no mcp measurements, so it is identical across tasks); Level-2 = the schema text tool_catalog.disclosed(role) already renders; the active ordering is applied in the spawn.py function that renders disclosed tools into the prompt (find it as the caller of tool_catalog.disclosed and name it in the docs), with an acceptance test asserting the stable block precedes the schemas only in active mode. (5) Skills: catalog_block is prepended inside spawn._prepare_skills as before; both cache_mode keys validated by the S2d1 helper pattern (a small cache_mode(cfg, section) in tool_catalog/skill_router, invalid -> off with invalid_config on the row).
Spec review T-1298 folded in (overrides earlier wording where they differ): (1) decision_log.last_row matches the role stored at deterministic.role (neither writer passes a top-level role). (2) last_row reads today's and yesterday's decision_log files (Europe/Zurich dates), still bounded; when neither has a qualifying row, changed_since_previous is None and the docs state it. (3) Codex rows: bus.log_run keeps writing per event, so the scorecard dedupes by subject (latest row per task) before computing counts, means and the changed share; the Level-0 catalog for codex_execute is tool_catalog.level0 over the CODEX_TOOLS ids (stable_catalog_chars may be small but never undefined). (4) No prompt renderer for tools exists today (the callers of tool_catalog.disclosed only build rows; the escalation writer at spawn.py near 1492 stays untouched): active tool cache_mode adds a packet section named tools inside spawn._packet_body, stable Level-0 catalog lines first, then the Level-2 schema text for the kept ids; in shadow the section is absent; the acceptance test asserts that ordering in active and absence in shadow. (5) One shared validator: context_router.cache_mode is generalised to cache_mode(cfg, section) (context_router, tool_disclosure, skills) and reused by all three callers; invalid values fall back to off and set invalid_config on the corresponding row; cache_mode is inert when the section's own mode (promotion.mode) is off. (6) pool.toml gains cache_mode keys in [tool_disclosure] and [skills] with dated comments and revert instructions; tests/test_pool.py joins the scope and covers the new keys. (7) Scorecard summary: per role; changed share = changed True / (True + False) with the None count printed separately; date range from row ts as ISO dates in Europe/Zurich; zero rows prints 'no tool_disclosure rows in range'; the CLI test asserts these exact fields. (8) Add a test that deterministic.kept and the new char fields survive decision_log._bounded for a row with 200 kept ids.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_tool_catalog.py::test_cache_view_stable_across_tasks_and_changed_flag_none_first (identical stable text for two tasks of a role; changed flag None without a previous row, True/False with one)

result.summary: The diff matches the acceptance criteria as far as I could check. I read the source and did not run the tests or the gate. Two medium concerns remain. Neither breaks a criterion, but both are worth fixing.

comments.issue: The skills catalog is prepended whenever skills.cache_mode is active, but nothing checks the [skills] mode. With mode=shadow (today's pool.toml) and cache_mode=active, the worker sees a catalog-only skills section, which breaks the shadow-first rule that a worker sees nothing new until the section is active. Spec item (5) only requires inertness when mode is off, so this is arguably compliant. Gating on mode==active, or at least mode!=off, would be safer. Also confirm that a skills mode of off never reaches this code.

level2() reads _SCHEMAS, which is filled as a side effect of _mcp_measurements() at import time. Any failure or ordering change in that scan silently switches dynamic_chars and the packet's schema text to the 'schema supplied by the worker harness' fallback. That would make the telemetry and the active-mode prompt differ without any signal. Consider building _SCHEMAS explicitly, or returning it from the measurement function.

The Claude-role row's 'dropped' is now computed as offered minus selected instead of choice['drop']. It can differ from the previous semantics, for example under specialist hand-over or when choice['drop'] excludes mandatory tools. This changes an existing field's meaning for consumers such as scorecards or routing readers, and no test pins it.

last_row reads a 200-line tail of the shared decisions.jsonl and then keeps only rows from today and yesterday. Busy logs can push the last same-role tool_disclosure row out of the window, so changed_since_previous silently becomes None. The docs state the None case, but the busy-log cause should be stated too. Also, the dated decisions-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl paths are guesses at a layout the writers don't produce; check them against how decision_log writes files.

The summary applies days as a since_ts cutoff, and the row-count dedupe uses (role, subject). The dedupe is fine. The CLI --days default and the output as space-joined key=value text are not obviously covered by the exact-field assertions in spec item (7). Confirm the test asserts the printed field names, including none_count and the 'no tool_disclosure rows in range' string.
